name: Daddy's Workshop of the Carolinas
old_description: Our lives are filled with all sorts of products, most of which come from the cogs of mass production, from a faraway land with little connection to people or place. This type of existence disconnects us from one another, how things are made & where they come from. I’d like to remedy that problem by reconnecting you to the human touch of natural materials. In an age where many things exist only in digital worlds, I hearken back to a more human time with natural wood worked & styled by a craftsman. You deserve something better than crumbling particle-board furniture. We can design from scratch, or work from a picture. I work mostly in the Craftsman & Shaker styles; furniture traditions that reflect an honest, solid way of life. Take a tour of my shop & furniture projects with the video & slideshow below. Coupled with making fine furniture, I also restore vintage machinery, with its elegant design & robust quality. From Grandma knitting in her rocker, to a child building with blocks by the fireplace, there is something deeply satisfying & richly human about creating things by hand. Join me in this long tradition of treasuring the physicality & humanness of working wood one piece at a time.
about:
Based in Lancaster, South Carolina, Daddy's Workshop of the Carolinas is operated by Joshua Pauling, who also serves as vicar, headmaster, and teacher at All Saints Lutheran Church and All Saints Classical Academy. The workshop began as a personal pursuit of hand-crafted furniture and vintage machinery restoration.

The shop produces custom furniture primarily in the Craftsman and Shaker styles, offering design from scratch or working from customer-provided images. In addition to furniture making, Pauling restores vintage woodworking machinery, emphasizing the elegant design and robust quality of older equipment. Operations are conducted on a small scale, with each piece built by hand using natural wood.

The workshop serves individual clients seeking bespoke furniture pieces and those requiring restoration of antique woodworking tools. No specific industry sectors or commercial customer types are identified in the company's public materials.

Pauling frames the work as a response to mass-produced, disposable goods, aiming to reconnect people with the human touch of natural materials and the satisfaction of creating things by hand. The venture reflects a philosophy that values the physicality and humanness of traditional woodworking.
